children.translated_text: <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s> (Lamp of <s>Abhidharma</s>)
Together with the <s>Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti</s> (Commentary with the Light of Vibhāṣā).
First chapter, first section.
He who revealed the path of cessation of suffering and its cause to humans and gods—

children.text: taṃ satpathajñaṃ praṇipatya buddhaṃ śāstraṃ kariṣyāmyabhidharmadīpam // [1] //
children.translated_text: Having bowed to that <s>Buddha</s>, the knower of the true path, I shall compose the treatise <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s> (Lamp of Abhidharma). [1]
If there were no change in beings and such, the absence of manifestation would follow;
Due to the transformation of that, the nature of being transformed belongs to <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), since there is non-difference from that. [2]
There is no action due to the abandonment of one's own nature; knowledge, manifestation, selfhood, and impurities—
In the first position, there is absence of liberation, and in the second, there are other calamities as well. [3]
The <s>rūpa-skandha</s> (form aggregate) indeed consists of the eye and other ten <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) and <s>dhātus</s> (elements);
Three <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) are designated as <s>dharma</s> (mental objects), together with <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest form); these three are permanent. [4]
The other one designated as <s>manas</s> (mind) comprises seven consciousness-elements;
<s>Āyatana</s> (sense base) is etymologically explained as the door of entry; <s>dhātu</s> (element) is explained as lineage. [5]
Due to suitability for meditative practice and other reasons, the Sage taught the twelve <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases);
And for those who conceive of oneness of intellect and so forth, He taught the eighteen <s>dhātus</s> (elements). [6]
Because the sixth (<s>manas</s>) depends on others, that which is the cause is <s>manas</s> (mind);
Due to the existence of the support of form and formless, the materiality of the five is declared. [7]
The inclusion of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), and <s>dhātus</s> (elements) by their own nature is taught;
Due to perpetual non-separation from their own nature, there is equality of <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caitasas</s> (mental factors). [8]
Those mentioned by those names in other <s>sūtras</s>—their inclusion in these very categories
Should be stated by one skilled in the method of the treatise, having considered their own characteristics. [9]
The mutual inclusion of <s>skandhas</s> and the rest should be understood according to appropriateness;
There is no inclusion of permanent entities in the <s>skandhas</s>, because they do not fall into the time periods and so forth. [10]
The inclusion of the eighty thousand <s>dharma-skandhas</s> (collections of teachings)
Should be understood as being within the points of entry, since by them one enters the true path. [11]
The measure of a <s>dharma-skandha</s> (collection of teachings), however, is a single discourse on truth and the like;
But its true nature, according to some, is even considered by others to be a word or name. [12]
The fundamental basis for the designation of a being is considered to be the six <s>dhātus</s> (elements);
They are taught because from their division, in this, <s>māra</s> (the Evil One, i.e., conceit) is turned back. [13]
'Because it is nourished by <s>satkāya-dṛṣṭi</s> (the view of the existing body)'—
The space element is distinct from <s>ākāśa</s> (space), due to its inclusion in the <s>rūpa-āyatana</s> (form sense base). [14]
Indeed, only defiled consciousness [should be regarded] as the basis of birth;

children.text: nabhaḥ khalu nabho dhātorāsanno hetureṣa tu /
children.translated_text: The sky indeed—the sky-element is close to this, but this is the cause;
Of the great elements, those belong to that which is born from them; this form belongs to the mind. [15]
That which has direct perceptual activity, and that which even grasps what has not been reached,
And that which apprehends an object more distant, is more firmly established than the other. [16]

children.text: abhidharmadīpe vimāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau prathamā(mā) dhyāsya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s> commentary, the second section of the first chapter.
Third section of the first chapter.
The first meaning is 'with-pointing-out' (<s>sanidarśana</s>); the material ones, ten, are 'with-resistance' (<s>sapratigha</s>);
Except for form and sound, those very same are considered morally indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>). [17]
The rest are of three kinds; here all in the <s>rūpa-dhātu</s> (form realm) are fourteen,
Excluding the two elements of taste and smell together with their consciousness—the last three. [18]
The last three are with-influx and without-influx (<s>sāsrava</s> and <s>anāsrava</s>); the rest are only with-influx;
The first five have objects (<s>sālamba</s>); with qualification, three are of three kinds. [19]
Memory is a mental state; the first is an earlier one, the second is intellectual in nature. [20]
Non-conceptual, having qualities, and self-referent—because there is no determination from the absence of self-conceit;
The five consciousnesses in the desire realm, with one, are conceptual (<s>savikalpaka</s>);
Other than that, in meditation with three, in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), there is also the non-concentrated. [21]
With two, undistracted; with one, having the eye, ear, and body as support;
With two, above that, distracted; with one alone, concentrated. [22]
For one whose wholesome seeds are cut off, perception is conceptual;
There is no wholesome consciousness except at the moment of rebirth-linking. [23]
For an ordinary person who is detached from the sense desires and who is subject to decline,
There is no unwholesome in either way; and for a noble one, there is no highest defiled. [24]
There is no undefiled-indeterminate that is conceptual of the higher realms;
Nor is there defiled conceptual consciousness that has the lower realms as its object. [25]
Here there are three kinds, and for a noble one, two; for one with attachment and merit,

children.text: na śubhaṃ nāpi ca kliṣṭaṃ dvitīyādiṣu darśakam // [26] //
children.translated_text: Neither wholesome nor defiled is a perceiver in the second and subsequent stages. [26]
Through application, through proximity of the limb, through homogeneity, and through continuity,
Memory arises in the mind regarding an object previously experienced by consciousness. [27]
From the reverse of this, due to dullness, and from being overpowered by affliction and disease,
Forgetfulness arises regarding things previously known. [28]
What was seen by the mind in two, three, four, or five modes
Is remembered by that and by others; but one does not see another's [experience] when the connection and vision cease. [29]
What is experienced by one of the five consciousnesses
Is also remembered by another; therefore, by the others as well. [30]
What was experienced as indeterminate in two ways—here the mind is twelve-fold;
Due to the cessation of the form and formless realms, it is remembered by only eight. [31]
What was attained by the wholesome of the cessation of the form and formless realms, in sequence,
Excluding the indeterminate attained in the desire realm, is remembered by ten. [32]
But in the form realm, what was seen by the indeterminate called 'unrestrained',
Excluding the formless-indeterminate, is remembered again by the others. [33]
What was known by the formless-indeterminate—that mind by nine,
Excluding the desire-realm-attained-indeterminate and the form-realm-attained-unrestrained, likewise. [34]
Seven called 'mind' (<s>citta</s>) have objects; the one called '<s>dharma</s>' is associated;
The immaterial ones together with sound are unappropriated—nine are of two kinds. [35]

children.text: spṛśyaṃ dvidhā sadharmāṃśāḥ saha tā nava bhautikāḥ /
children.translated_text: The tangible is of two kinds; those with a <s>dharma</s> portion—together, nine are material-element-derived;

children.text: daśa sāvayavā mūrtāḥ ta eva daśa saṃcitāḥ // [36] //
children.translated_text: Ten have parts and are material; those very ten are compounded. [36]
Form, smell, taste, and touch are considered to have the nature of cutter and cuttable;
They are burners and weighers; and they are burnable and weighable as well. [37]
The five are of the nature of material sense faculties, consisting of <s>vipāka</s> (fruition) and accumulation;
The immaterial ones are not of accumulation; the rest are of three kinds; sound is of two kinds. [38]
The eye and the apprehension of that—does one obtain them separately or together?
Twelve are known as internal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>); the external ones are of six objective natures. [39]
The last three are of three kinds; the rest are destroyed on the path of cultivation;
There is no form that is this visible, nor undefiled, nor non-conceptual. [40]
Only the homogeneous is called '<s>dharma</s>'; the rest are taught as being of both kinds;
The homogeneous, in its state of homogeneity, is likened to one's own activity. [41]
The eye together with the <s>dharma-dhātu</s> portion—<s>dṛṣṭi</s> (view) is spoken of in nine ways;
The wisdom of the five consciousnesses is not <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (view), because it does not discriminate. [42]
Just as the eye sees what is visible on cloudy and cloudless nights and days,
So too the defiled and undefiled views, and the learner and adept, perceive. [43]

children.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau prathamasyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s> commentary, the third section of the first chapter.
Fourth section of the first chapter.
The eye sees and consciousness cognizes its own domain;
Due to the difference between mere seeing and apprehension, the distinction between the two is very great. [44]
Is the function of one eye consciousness, or of both eyes?
<s>Manas</s> (mind), the eye, and the ear—three—grasp their objects without contact; the others do otherwise. [45]
Those that grasp without contact are established, due to their grasping from far, near, and equal distances;
If it be through the power of a lamp and such, no, because it does not arise equally from that. [46]
If there would be the consequence of grasping everything—no, from the observation of a magnet and such;
If there is no fault because of omnipresence—no, because of non-connection, like sesame and oil. [47]

children.text: na hyū rdhvaṃ cakṣuṣaḥ kāyo na rūpaṃ nākṣijaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: The body is not above the eye; form is not; nor is mind born from the eye;

children.text: vijñānasya tu netrārthastau ca kāyasya savaṃtaḥ // [48] //
children.translated_text: But for consciousness, the eye and the object—and both are everywhere for the body. [48]

children.text: nopariṣṭācchru teḥ kāyo na śabdo na svakaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: The body is not above the ear; sound is not; nor is one's own mind;

children.text: vijñānasya tu nihrādastau ca kāyasya sarvataḥ // [49] //
children.translated_text: But for consciousness, it is sound; and both are everywhere for the body. [49]
For the three, all three are their own; but for the body, consciousness is also below;
<s>Manas</s> (mind), however, is unrestricted—the sovereign nature of the yogin has been shown. [50]
Those <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) that are with-influx and without-influx which are designated as <s>upādāna</s> (clinging)—
They should be known as only with-influx, due to their assistance, action, and so forth. [51]
Time periods and such are synonyms of <s>skandha</s> (aggregate); <s>dharma</s> and such are synonyms of an existent thing;
But those that are designated as 'with-influx' are taught by names such as <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) and so forth. [52]
Due to the oneness of own nature, object, and function, by a single element;
Even though the eye and such are divided into two, the dual derivation is due to the threefold nature of action. [53]
Due to the distinction of being uncommon, due to sovereignty, and due to being internal,
Even though there are multiple causes, consciousness is distinguished by those. [54]
Due to being permanent and being wholesome, <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is truly a real substance;
By that essential substance, the one called '<s>dharma</s>' is considered to possess substance. [55]
The first pure mind—from its rarity, a moment is taught;
By that wondrous moment, these last three are momentary. [56]
The nose, tongue, and body—these three grasp objects of equal kind;
The support of the last is past; and for the five, it is also together with those. [57]
Depending on the <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary meditation) or the four absorptions,
The eye-element is ceased through the path that is without-influx (<s>anāsrava</s>). [58]
Depending on <s>anāgamya</s>, the smell-element is ceased;
The mind-element ceases through <s>anāgamya</s> or through seven supports. [59]
<s>Anāgamya</s> likewise is the first—that called eye-consciousness;
Due to the variety of the <s>dharma-dhātu</s> (dharma element), one should explain according to the appropriate connection. [60]
When an ordinary person fully comprehends the eye-element attained in the form realm,
He attains detachment from the entire element consisting of form. [61]
Therefore, he abandons thirty-one latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) from the element,
But at that time he does not eliminate any fetter (<s>saṃyojana</s>). [62]
He attains detachment from form and abandons three latent tendencies;

children.text: tadā saṃyojanaṃ tvāryaḥ paryādatte na kiñcanā // [63] //
children.translated_text: But at that time, a noble one does not eliminate any fetter. [63]
When fully comprehending the eye-consciousness-element, that very one
Necessarily also fully comprehends and becomes detached from the <s>Brahmaloka</s> (Brahmā-world). [64]

children.text: na tu saṃyojanaṃ kiñcitparyādatte tadā hyasau /
children.translated_text: But he does not eliminate any fetter at that time;
When an ordinary person fully comprehends the smell-element and the one called taste, [65]
He certainly attains detachment from the desire realm, and even the latent tendencies—
At that time he abandons thirty-six, and the three fetters. [66]
A noble one, however, accomplishes detachment from desires, and even the latent tendencies—
He fully comprehends four and also eliminates three. [67]
When fully comprehending the mind-element, one becomes detached from the formless realms;
One abandons thirty latent tendencies and eliminates three likewise. [68]
When fully comprehending joy (<s>prīti</s>), one abandons that very thing;

children.text: ābhāsvarācca vairāgyaṃ yāti hanti tu nāsravān // [69] //
children.translated_text: And one goes to detachment from <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (the Radiant heaven), but does not destroy the influxes. [69]
When the yogin fully comprehends happiness (<s>sukha</s>), he abandons that here;

children.text: śubhakṛtsnācca vairāgyaṃ yāti kleśānna hanti tu // [70] //
children.translated_text: And he goes to detachment from <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (the heaven of Complete Beauty), but does not destroy the afflictions. [70]

children.text: dvivijñeyāḥ guṇāḥ pañca hetuḥ sarve kṣarākṣarāḥ /
children.translated_text: Qualities are to be known as twofold in five; all causes are perishable and imperishable;
Except for the objects of the <s>dharma-dhātu</s>—the six external are not of the nature of sense faculties. [71]
In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s> [commentary, the first chapter.]
Second chapter, first section.
Of the twenty-two kinds of the entire section on <s>indriyas</s> (faculties),
The <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) beginning with etymology shall be explained in brief. [72]

children.text: nāmnā dvāviṃśatistāni dravyato daśa sapta ca /
children.translated_text: By name they are twenty-two; by substance, seventeen;
Because the other two are not different from their function—the triad of nine beginning with pleasure. [73]
Due to the absence of a valid defining characteristic from the name, and due to the meaningfulness of that name,
Although the three function as a group, the meaning is sought by others. [74]
Due to being the cause of distinguished cognition, and due to the distinction of sovereignty,
The superiority of the two over the body-faculty is like that of the eye-faculty and so forth. [75]
The meaning of <s>indriya</s> (faculty) is declared by the wise to be sovereignty;
For the five, in the instances of their own objects; for the four, however, in both objects. [76]
Others know the mastery in the apprehension of their own objects and so forth;
Still others, who consider themselves learned, say it is only in the consciousness of their own objects. [77]
In the arising of afflictions for pleasure and the like, and in the attainment of virtues for faith and the like,
The sequence is due to the nature of fruit, defilement, accumulation, and purification. [78]
Those by which the designation of 'being', the variety of beings, steadfastness, and the arising of afflictions,
The means to the path, and the attainment of the fruit [occur]—their faculty-nature (<s>indriyatā</s>) is recognized. [79]
Fourteen are due to being the support, origin, basis, and experience of contact;
The other eight faculties are due to being the cause of heaven and liberation. [80]
Desire is because it is a limb of effort; contact is because it nourishes feeling;
Perception, because it is overpowered by wisdom—the Sage did not declare it a faculty. [81]

children.text: śraddhādīnāṃ vidāṃ caiva doṣaḥ śuddhau malodaye /
children.translated_text: For faith and the rest and for the knowers too, the fault in purification and the arising of impurity—
Due to being primary, attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) is not declared a faculty. [82]
Due to being favorable to conviction, <s>adhimokṣa</s> (resolve) also is not a faculty.
Because of the two [objections of] doubt regarding the arising of fruit at a different time, it is not <s>cetanā</s> (volition) // [83] //
Nor is it <s>apramāda</s> (heedfulness), because of [being subsumed by] <s>vīrya</s> (energy); nor is it <s>hrī</s> (modesty), because of the restraint of boldness,
Nor is it <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), nor <s>alobha</s> (non-greed), because they are subsumed by <s>vīrya</s> (energy) and <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) // [84] //
It is not <s>praśrabdhi</s> (tranquility) because of agitation in knowledge; and the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) are not [included] because of being blameworthy,
<s>Jāti</s> (birth) and others are not [included] because they serve another purpose; <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) is not because of being inactive // [85] //

children.text: kāyasya bādhanaṃ duḥkhaṃ daurmanasyaṃ tu cetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Duḥkha</s> (suffering) is the affliction of the body, while <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure) belongs to the mind,

children.text: sukhaṃ ca sumanastā ca sātaṃ śārīramānasam // [86] //
children.translated_text: <s>Sukha</s> (pleasure) and <s>sumanastā</s> (mental satisfaction) are agreeable feelings, bodily and mental respectively // [86] //
Because of its superiority, mental agreeable feeling is sometimes called <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) // [87ab] //
The <s>indriya</s> (faculty) beginning with the stainless one should be understood as existing in six planes,
Others besides that, belonging to the pure faculties, should be seen as existing in nine planes // [88] //
<s>Daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure) is to be abandoned in two ways; the three mental feelings are [abandoned] in three ways,
Nine are to be abandoned through cultivation; [five] are of two kinds, but not the three // [89] //
First, in the desire realm, <s>vipāka</s> (retribution) through those arising sequentially is obtained as twofold,

children.text: anyaiḥ ṣaṭ sapta vāṣṭau vā ṣaḍ rūpe antye tu jīvitam // [90] //
children.translated_text: With the others, six, seven, or eight; six in the form realm; but in the last, only the life faculty // [90] //
For the dying, three cease at the end; eight in the intermediate [state],

children.text: daśāṣṭau nava catvāri kāme pañca śubhāni vā // [91] //
children.translated_text: Ten, eight, nine, four, or five wholesome ones in the desire realm // [91] //

children.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau dvitīyasyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the commentary called <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>, the first quarter of the second chapter //
Second chapter, second quarter /
The acquisition of the first and last is with nine; and of the two middle ones with seven or eight,
But acquisition with eleven occurs from the loss of the final fruit // [92] //
Full understanding of one's own realm is through the path that sees its opposite // [93ab] //
Full understanding of the desire realm is generally considered to be through seven [faculties],
But with impure and pure faculties for the purpose, it is said to be through eight // [94] //
Full understanding of the form realm is considered to be through ten faculties,
Full understanding of the formless realm is said to be through eleven // [95] //
All beings dwelling in the three realms are endowed with <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), life force, and mind,
In the desire realm, [they possess] the sense of touch, femininity, and physical characteristics; form-realm beings [possess] the eye and other [faculties] // [96] //
Indeed, those in the desire realm [are endowed] with suffering; one attached to it, with mental displeasure,
But one born above [is endowed] with pleasure; a noble one, with the faculties called 'wholesome' in the lower two [realms] likewise // [97] //
Through joy, those born in the lower [realms of form]; with the wholesome [faculties], one who has wholesome roots,
With the two trainee [faculties], those on the path of liberation; [the non-learner, the <s>Arhat</s>], follows his own path // [98] //
One endowed with equanimity, life force, and mind is necessarily possessed of three [faculties],
One with bodily pleasure has four; one with sight has five // [99] //
One endowed with the female faculty and so on has eight; one in suffering is possessed of seven,
With eleven through the last two; one having the first of those has seven or six // [100] //
Those born in the three continents and in the hells, even those fixed in wrong views,
At most [are endowed]
with nineteen, at least with eight // [101] //
Intermediate beings, hungry ghosts, animals, and <s>śraddhānusārins</s> (faith-followers):
Are endowed with thirteen, or with nineteen // [102] //

children.text: samyaktvaniyatā ye tu ye ca śraddhādhimuktikāḥ /
children.translated_text: But those who are fixed in right views, and those who are <s>śraddhādhimuktikas</s> (freed through faith),
They are endowed with eleven, or with nineteen // [103] //
The <s>Arhat</s> called <s>prajñāvimukta</s> (liberated through wisdom), <s>kāyasākṣin</s> (body-witness), and <s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s> (liberated both ways),
Are equipped with eleven faculties, or endowed with eighteen // [104] //
The deceased desire-realm gods, at minimum with seventeen,
They are at most endowed with nineteen faculties // [105] //
But those born in the [first two]
<s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), at absolute minimum with fifteen,
Those in <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (the plane of total beauty) are endowed with fourteen // [106] //
Those in <s>Bṛhatphala</s> (the plane of great fruit) are endowed at minimum with thirteen,
But at maximum they are endowed with sixteen faculties // [107] //
The formless realm beings, at minimum with eight and at maximum with eleven,
Beings including the gods and <s>Uttarakurus</s> are endowed with thirteen // [108] //
One without wholesome [roots] is endowed with eight, or with thirteen,
Those of dual sex, at minimum with the latter ones, with twenty or twenty-one at most // [109] //
The <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom) going outward is inseparable from seven substances,
In the desire realm, one more in the body [sense]; two more in the eye and other [senses] // [110] //
Similarly in the form realm it should be known, except for the pair of smell and taste,

children.text: cittaṃ caitasikaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ tu svalakṣaṇaiḥ // [111] //
children.translated_text: <s>Citta</s> (mind) together with <s>caitasikas</s> (mental factors) is conditioned, with its own characteristics // [111] //

children.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau dvitīyasya [adhyāyasya] dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the commentary <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>, the second quarter of the second chapter //
Second chapter, third quarter /
The ten <s>dharmas</s> that are <s>mahābhaumikas</s> (universal mental factors) are: <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>cetanā</s> (volition), <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness),
<s>Chanda</s> (desire), <s>sparśa</s> (contact), <s>adhimokṣa</s> (resolve), <s>dhī</s> (wisdom), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>manaskṛti</s> (attention) // [112] //
<s>Śraddhā</s> (faith), <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), <s>apramāda</s> (heedfulness), <s>praśrabdhi</s> (tranquility), <s>hrī</s> (shame), <s>apatrapā</s> (decency),
The two roots [of non-greed and non-hatred], <s>vīrya</s> (energy), and <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence) — these are remembered as the ten <s>kuśala-mahābhūmikas</s> (wholesome universals) // [113] //
<s>Styāna</s> (torpor), <s>pramāda</s> (heedlessness), <s>āśraddhya</s> (faithlessness), <s>ālasya</s> (laziness), <s>mūḍhi</s> (delusion), <s>uddhava</s> (restlessness),

children.text: kliṣṭe ṣaṭ aśubhe tu dve āhrīkyamanapatrapā // [114] //
children.translated_text: These six are the <s>kleśa-mahābhūmikas</s> (defiled universals); but in the unwholesome, two: <s>āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness) and <s>anapatrapā</s> (recklessness) // [114] //
<s>Māyā</s> (deceit), <s>śāṭhya</s> (hypocrisy), <s>mada</s> (pride), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>vihiṃsā</s> (violence), <s>īrṣyā</s> (envy), and <s>pradāśa</s> (spite),
<s>Upanāha</s> (resentment) and <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness) — these are the ten <s>upakleśa-bhūmikas</s> (minor defilements) // [115] //
Just as substance such as earth is differentiated through connection with qualities such as blue,
So the mind is differentiated by those respective terms through connection with mental factors // [116] //
Just as the diversity of elements and elemental derivatives is not produced by their own nature,
So also should the distinctness of <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caittas</s> (mental factors) be understood // [117] //
Just as transformation in water is observed through connection with what is associated [with it],
So should the modification of consciousness through association with its associates be observed // [118] //
Quality, attribute, <s>dharma</s>, measure, function, and substratum —
These and similar terms operate with reference to a principal [entity] // [119] //
<s>Citta</s> (mind) is the principal among these, being the substantial entity through grasping of the mere [object] and so forth,
And this is the seed of activities, both of purification and defilement // [120] //
The [mind] that has reached the desire realm arises with twelve <s>dharmas</s>,
Undefiled-indeterminate mind [arises] like the sun with its rays // [121] //
Similarly, obscured mind arises with eighteen mental factors,
Wholesome mind necessarily occurs with twenty-two [factors] // [122] //
Unwholesome mind arises with twenty mental factors,
That which is connected only with wrong view and delusion; but one should say more with anger and so forth // [123] //
Since <s>middha</s> (sleep) can occur everywhere, wherever it exists it should be indicated,
And likewise <s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret) should sometimes be counted as additional // [124] //
Unwholesome <s>middha</s> (sleep) and <s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret) do not exist in the form realm,
In the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) [is absent]; and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought) also does not [exist] above // [125] //
An associated <s>saṃskāra</s> (formation) is one whose equality is fivefold,
And a dissociated one should be understood as that which lacks such equality // [126] //
There is no overextension to material forms because of the non-existence of a distinguished name,
And because of the inclusion under <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), [the objection regarding] space and others does not apply // [127] //
<s>Prāpti</s> (acquisition) and others are the thirteen dissociated <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations),
Their marks are the statements of the authoritative and their own activity; [these] marks will be explained // [128] //
<s>Prāpti</s> (acquisition) is [also called] <s>samanviti</s> (possession), <s>labdhi</s> (attainment), <s>dharmavatā</s> (having dharmas), and <s>vyavasthiti</s> (establishment) // [129ab] //
And [it applies] to those born of hearing and reflection, and to the two <s>samāpattis</s> (attainments) // [130cd] //
For the wholesome [dharmas], the defilement-conditioned unprecedented [acquisition] of those possessing impurities,

children.text: ādilābhe saha prākca tadūrdhvaṃ vā tridheṣyate // [131] //
children.translated_text: At the initial acquisition, simultaneously, before, or after — thus it is considered threefold // [131] //

children.text: kliṣṭāṇāṃ kuśalānāṃ ca tadanyeṣāṃ tridhā matā /
children.translated_text: For the defiled and the wholesome and others besides them, [acquisition] is considered threefold,
Similarly for the obscured-indeterminate [dharmas], and for minds of knowledge and creation // [132] //
For <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, at the initial attainment; for the other permanent [dharma, i.e. space], always,
Unborn and present, and sometimes — thus it is considered threefold // [133] //
That which is the cause of beings having similar purpose and inclination is <s>sabhāgatā</s> (homogeneous nature),
<s>Āsaṃjñika</s> (the unconscious state) is the retributive result, which is the cessation of mind in those who had perception // [134] //
The wholesome <s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s> (attainment of non-perception), which obstructs mind in the last <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation),
Because it does not operate from the desire for escape, it is not attainable by a noble one through effort // [135] //
But the one called <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) should be known as the highest of existences, for one who desires to be free,
It is wholesome, attainable through effort by a noble one, and considered unfixed with respect to two feelings // [136] //
Because of the non-engagement of the four aspects of consciousness, from scripture, and from reasoning,
Because of the state of mind being turned away — thus this state of no-mind is established // [137] //
<s>Āyus</s> (life force) is the basis for designation of a destiny, the sustainer of mind and warmth,
From scripture, from reasoning, and substantially — it is accepted as real // [138] //
<s>Jāti</s> (birth), <s>sthiti</s> (persistence), <s>jarā</s> (decay), and <s>nāśa</s> (destruction) are the four characteristics of the conditioned,
There are four [characteristics]; regarding persistence and destruction, [they exist] because the [opponents'] argument from causality etc. is not established // [139] //
The establishment of decay is through the diminution of power; it is not transformation due to otherness,
The diminution of power is established through single causation and destruction // [140] //
When birth exists, because of its existence; because of the destruction of substantial efficacy,
From scripture and from reasoning, destruction also has a cause // [141] //
Having their origin dependent on vocal sound, having the function of conveying their own meaning,
Called <s>saṃjñā</s> (name) and so forth — the three, <s>nāma</s> (name), [<s>pada</s> (sentence), and <s>vyañjana</s> (syllable)], are recognized // [142] //
<s>Nāma</s> (name) and others are different from sound, because of revealing a meaning not yet attained,
But they should be known as impermanent, because of manifesting meaning dependently // [143] //

children.text: svarūpaṃ vedayaṃścchabdo vyañjanā dīni ca dhruvam /
children.translated_text: Sound expresses its own nature, and syllables and others certainly [express theirs],
The wise say that [sound is] meaningful through the attribution of [conventional] designation // [144] //
Because of its atomic nature, oneness with articulated sound is not possible,
Identity [is not possible] because of being obstructive; this is established by obstruction and other [properties] // [145] //
No eternal sound called <s>sphoṭa</s> apart from articulated sound is established,
Through sound occurring in sequence, a particular meaning is expressed // [146] //

children.text: na śrutyā śrūyate śabdastadanyā ca gatiḥ śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: Sound is not heard by another hearing, and hearing has no function other than that,
One who would say [otherwise] would be laughed at by the wise // [147] //
What is to be revealed, as appropriate — and they [names etc.] are both fixed and unfixed,
Because of definitively manifesting [the truth], the <s>Buddha</s> is understood to be omniscient // [148] //
Those called <s>sattvākhyā</s> (pertaining to beings) are obtained in the desire and form [realms], and are likewise outflow-indeterminate,
And similarly <s>vipāka</s> (retribution) and <s>sābhāgya</s> (homogeneous) — [acquisitions are] of two kinds // [149] //

children.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau dvitīyasyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the commentary <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>, the third quarter of the second chapter //
The second chapter is completed //
Third chapter / Fourth quarter /
Because of the absence of affliction called <s>sattvākhya</s> (pertaining to beings) in the fourth [realm], there is none according to the <s>sūtra</s>,
Since the aerial palace of equality is destroyed, how can there be permanence? // [150] //
Seven [destructions] by fire, one by water; when the seven [cycles] of water are gone, again,
After the seven cycles by fire, one [destruction] by wind [follows] // [151] //
After the sevenfold [destruction] by fire, one by wind — what comes next?
Because of the taking up of lifespan, thus the increase of lifespan in <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (the plane of total beauty) // [152] //
Because of similarity with faults such as wind [disorders] of beings, [these are their destroyers],
Because of resemblance, [these are called] internal; [earth] is not considered a world-destroying [element] // [153] //

children.text: abhidharmadīpe [vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau tṛtīyasyādhyāyasya ca]turthaḥ pādaḥ samāptaḥ //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, [in the commentary <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>, the] fourth quarter [of the third chapter] is completed //
The third chapter is completed
Fourth chapter / First quarter /
Of the causes of the arising and birth of beings, [which are the] arrangers of fortune and misfortune,
<s>Karma</s> (action) is accepted as the cause, being the creators of the diversity of the world // [154] //

children.text: kāyikaṃ vāṅmayaṃ caiva cetanākhyaṃ ca mānasam /

children.translated_text: These <s>karmas</s> (actions) are the cause of the world, not <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and others / [155] //
Bodily, verbal, and mental — called <s>cetanā</s> (volition),
No dependence on [God is needed]; the practice of austerity [would be pointless], due to faults such as partiality / [156] //
Because of diversity, because of sequential arising, because of the consequence of otherwise being similar,
The power of <s>karmas</s> (actions) is understood through rules, time, accumulation, and other [factors],
Therefore the designation applied to them is used in a secondary sense // [157] //
In the former [bodily and verbal actions], there are <s>vijñapti</s> (manifest action) and <s>avijñapti</s> (unmanifest action); <s>cetanā</s> (volition) is the mental action // [158] //

children.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau caturthādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the commentary <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s>, the first quarter of the fourth chapter
Fourth chapter, second quarter /
Just as food excessively burnt by fire, and a pot that has been processed,
So is the moral discipline of one with wrong views, whose self is damaged by hypocrisy, envy, and the like // [159] //
Conventionally, endowed with right view, is <s>bhikṣutva</s> (monkhood); in the ultimate sense,
One success is conventional; in the absence of both, it is neither // [160] //
In knowledge free from obstruction, the primary designation from the <s>Buddha's</s> statement,
And in the fruit that depends on that, the designation of quality should be known // [161] //
Because of eternity and purity, and because of the cessation of all suffering,
By primary designation, similarly <s>Dharma</s> is said to be <s>Nirvāṇa</s> // [162] //
The noble ones, the qualities of disciples — <s>Saṃgha</s> similarly in the ultimate sense,

children.text: etānyo yāti śaraṇaṃ sa yāti śaraṇatrayam // [163] //
children.translated_text: One who goes to these for refuge goes to the threefold refuge // [163] //
Wrong conduct is condemned by the good, because of the attainment of misfortune in the next life,
False speech because of being the most sinful; drinking liquor because of the loss of mindfulness // [164] //
From all present [karmas], from both types, that born of desire,
But from the fundamental [karmas] of the three times, the two born of meditation are obtained // [165] //
Restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) from all classes of beings is through speech and body as causes;
not from all limbs of restraint and beings through [all] causes. [166]
The attainment of non-restraint (<s>asaṃvara</s>) is through action, or through [mere] acceptance;
the <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest action) is distinct due to differences of field, limbs, and so on. [167]
Abandonment of the restraint obtained in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) is through renouncing the precepts (<s>śikṣā</s>) and the like;
some say through committing a <s>pātanīya</s> (defeating) offense; others deny this, due to disconnection. [168]
Due to disconnection, like a cloth whose threads are destroyed, the material substance perishes;
the mention of destruction in the <s>sūtra</s> has another meaning, as in [the case of] envy, hypocrisy, and so on. [169]
When the true <s>Dharma</s> has disappeared, some [say] others [cannot obtain it] due to non-attainment of what has not existed before;

children.text: bhūsaṃcāreṇa hānyā ca tyajyate dhyānajaṃ śubham // [170] //
children.translated_text: and by traversing [lower] grounds, the wholesome [karma] born of <s>dhyāna</s> is lost. [170]
Likewise, that obtained in the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>), for noble ones (<s>ārya</s>), through attainment of the fruit, destruction of faculties, and other [means];
non-restraint (<s>asaṃvara</s>) is [abandoned] through self-control, abandoning one's life, and so on. [171]
But the intermediate <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest action) is [lost] through interruptions of mental impulse and the like;
what is called wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>) obtained in the desire realm [is lost] by three [means]: cutting the roots, and so on. [172]
The defiled [avijñapti] is lost through the arising of its antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>);
that obtained in the three realms is lost; all [are present] in the desire realm, twelve in the form realm, one in the formless realm through attainment. [173]
That action which gives a desired fruit is declared wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>);
the opposite is unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>); and the indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) is otherwise. [174]
The first [karma] obtained in the desire realm is meritorious (<s>puṇya</s>); demeritorious (<s>apuṇya</s>) has an unwholesome nature;
that belonging to higher realms is imperturbable (<s>ānejya</s>), since its ripening (<s>vipāka</s>) is not agitated. [175]
Wholesome (<s>śubha</s>) action is to be experienced as pleasant, from <s>dhyāna</s> up to below the fourth;
elsewhere it is to be experienced as equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>); but unwholesome is to be experienced as suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>). [176]

children.text: adho 'pi madhyamaṃ karma dhyānenā ntyepi nirvṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: Below also, moderate action [leads to] contentment through <s>dhyāna</s>; also in the last [realm],
the desired [result] of threefold ripening simultaneously is due to the ripening of intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>. [177]
Again, <s>karma</s> is fourfold by the division of 'experienced in this life' (<s>dṛṣṭavedya</s>) and so on;
except for that called 'experienced in the present life,' the [other] three give rise to rebirth. [178]
And there is projection by all four everywhere, except in the hells (<s>naraka</s>);
for there, since there is no desired fruit, wholesome [karma] does not ripen. [179]
One who creates karma to be experienced at birth does not do so there, [for] an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) detached [from that realm];
a noble one (<s>ārya</s>) is firm, nor does another do [so]; though unstable also at the root of existence. [180]
When action is performed frequently with a tender or fierce mind,

children.text: satkṣetre kriyate yacca phalaṃ tasya niyamyate // [181] //
children.translated_text: and what is done in a good field (<s>satkṣetra</s>)—its fruit is determined. [181]
Due to the distinction of field and intention (<s>āśaya</s>), the fruit ripens immediately;
and upon arising from cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) attainment, etc., there is the immediate-time fruit action. [182]
Because of non-arising again in that ground, and what is determined as to ripening (<s>vipāka</s>)—
that should be known as fruit experienced in this life; the action below it is the supplementary one. [183]
The feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) of wholesome [karma] without deliberation is only mental (<s>caitasikī</s>);
but the desired bodily [feeling] is the ripening of action to be experienced as suffering. [184]
The unwholesome with ripening is 'black' (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>); that born in the form realm with ripening is 'white' (<s>śukla</s>);
wholesome-and-unwholesome is twofold in the desire realm; the 'pure' (<s>nirmala</s>) is that which causes their abandonment. [185]
The four paths of seeing (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) are through the path of volition (<s>cetanā</s>) and meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>);
the uninterrupted paths (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>) in the desire realm—this is the <s>karma</s> that destroys the 'black.' [186]

children.text: navame cetanā yā tu sā kṛṣṇākṛṣṇayā [ghā]tinī /
children.translated_text: The volition (<s>cetanā</s>) that is in the ninth [path] is the destroyer of both black and non-black;
[at] the uninterrupted path and the path of liberation, in each <s>dhyāna</s>, [it destroys] the 'white.' [187]
All unwholesome <s>karma</s> of body, etc., is considered misconduct (<s>duścarita</s>);
and also the three—covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>), etc.—are the three mental misconducts. [188]
Their wholesome counterpart—non-covetousness, etc.—is declared the three good conducts (<s>sucarita</s>);
both [sets] are the root; below that is <s>karma</s>; the ten paths are wholesome and unwholesome. [189]
In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s> commentary, the second quarter of the fourth chapter.
Third quarter of the fourth chapter.
Six <s>avijñapti</s>s (non-manifest actions) made by two [types]—those same six are performed;

children.text: śubhāḥ sapta dvidhā jñeyā ekavai(dhai)te samāhitāḥ // [190] //
children.translated_text: seven wholesome ones are to be known as twofold—those established in concentration (<s>samāhita</s>). [190]
The <s>avijñapti</s> in the preliminary stages, but the opposite in the subsequent stages;
the preparatory effort (<s>prayoga</s>) arises from three roots; [<s>abhidhyā</s>, etc., arise from three roots]. [191]
Wholesome preparatory and subsequent ones arise from the three wholesome roots
through hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), the completion of killing, harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>), and malice (<s>vyāpatti</s>). [192]
Theft, going to another's wife, and covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>)—from greed (<s>lobha</s>);
wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>)—from delusion (<s>moha</s>); for the others, it is held to be from [all] three. [193]
The basis (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of the four should be known in order as follows:

children.text: prāṇinaścātha bhogāśca nāmarūpaṃ ca nāma ca // [194] //
children.translated_text: living beings, possessions, name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>), and name. [194]
Taking life (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>) is intentionally, without mistake, killing another;
taking what is not given (<s>adattādāna</s>) is said to be taking another's unabandoned property. [195]
Sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>) is intercourse with another's wife, which involves deliberation;
speaking otherwise than what is known in meaning is false speech (<s>mṛṣāvacas</s>), with the intention to deceive. [196]
What is grasped by sight, hearing, and other senses, and by the mind—
is called 'seen, heard, cognized, and known' (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>, <s>śruta</s>, <s>mata</s>, <s>jñāta</s>) respectively, in that order. [197]
Divisive speech (<s>paiśunya</s>) is speech that causes division; harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>) is what is unpleasant;
idle talk (<s>saṃbhinnalāpitva</s>) is defiled—others [say it is] like songs, stories, and the like. [198]
Covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) is the desire for another's property that is not rightfully one's own; malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>) has beings as its object,
with hostility; wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) is the view that denies causality. [199]
Volition (<s>cetanā</s>) is not the action-path; but through them, existence continues;
simultaneously with as many as eight unwholesome volitions. [200]
With wholesome ones, up to ten; the partial ones are with one, eight, or five;
lamentation, hatred, and harsh speech exist in the hells (<s>naraka</s>) in two ways. [201]
Likewise, covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) is considered so, and wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) likewise;
similarly, the triad of covetousness, etc.; in <s>Kuru</s>, idle talk is in two ways. [202]
But the ten unwholesome ones exist elsewhere everywhere; the three wholesome ones exist everywhere;
for those in the formless realm, noble ones (<s>ārya</s>), and the unconscious realm, the seven embodied ones [exist] through attainment. [203]
Excluding <s>Kuru</s> and the hells, everywhere else they are twofold;
all ten give rise to ripening fruit (<s>vipākaphala</s>), outflow fruit (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>), and predominance fruit (<s>adhipatyaphala</s>). [204]
Suffering from being connected with suffering; short lifespan from killing;
emaciation from destroying vitality—this is the threefold fruit of that. [205]
Karma on the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>) has fruit with five fruits;
for the noble one with the pure [path], with four; likewise with other wholesome and unwholesome [karmas]. [206]
Other than that, the pure should be known with three; the indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) likewise;

children.text: phalaṃ śubhasya catvāri dvetrīṇi ca śubhādayaḥ // [207] //
children.translated_text: the fruits of the wholesome are four, two, and three respectively. [207]

children.text: śubhādyāstvaśubhasya dve trīṇi catvāri ca kramāt /
children.translated_text: For the unwholesome, from the wholesome, etc., [there are] two, three, and four in order;

children.text: avyākṛtasya te tu dve trīṇi trīṇi śubhādayaḥ // [208] //
children.translated_text: for the indeterminate, from the wholesome, etc., they are two, three, and three. [208]
All [give] four for the past and the middle [i.e., present]; and for the future,
two for one's own in the middle; three for the non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) birth. [209]
Four for the single-ground, or two; three for those of other grounds;
the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), etc., [give] three for the learner's [karma]; those same for the non-learner's (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) karma. [210]

children.text: ekaṃ trīṇi dvayaṃ caiva śaikṣādyāḥ paścimasya tu /
children.translated_text: One, three, and two from the learner, etc., for the last one;

children.text: dve dve pañca yathāsaṃkhyaṃ dṛggheyasya tu karmaṇaḥ // [211] //
children.translated_text: two, two, and five respectively for the karma to be abandoned by insight (<s>dṛgheya</s>). [211]

children.text: trīṇi catvāri caikaṃ ca dṛṣṭiheyādayaḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Three, four, and one—those abandoned by insight, etc., are remembered;

children.text: te tvabhyāsapraheyasya dve catvāri tridhā matāḥ // [212] //
children.translated_text: but for that to be abandoned by practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>)—two, four, and threefold is considered. [212]
In order: one, two, and four for the karma not to be abandoned;
by one [karma], birth is projected; by many, it is supplemented. [213]
Whether wholesome or unwholesome, the past [karma] that gives fruit—
one's own karma of body, speech, and mind—that is considered the ownership of karma (<s>karmasvakatā</s>). [214]
Conventionally (<s>saṃvṛtyā</s>), in the continuum of aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), from seeing the action and its fruit,

children.text: karttṛtā bhoktṛtā coktā niṣiddhā śāśvatasya tu // [215] //
children.translated_text: agency and experiencer-ship are spoken of; but the [view of] permanence (<s>śāśvata</s>) is denied. [215]
'There is ownership of karma, yet not so'—this is the fourfold [analysis];
the first is for one situated in its fruit, due to the loss of that karma. [216]
The second is for one situated in its fruit, due to the connection with that karma;
the third is for one endowed with both; the fourth is for one with neither. [217]
'There is ownership of karma, but one will not experience its fruit'—
the first should be known for one situated in the last fruit. [218]
The second is for one whose ripening is certain, but who is not established in its ripening;
the third is from the existence of both; the fourth is without both. [219]
'One may be connected with karma, yet not experience its fruit'—
the first is by karma whose ripening has been exhausted, by one ceased, future, etc. [220]
The second is by karma that is lost but has certain ripening;
the third is for one free from both; the fourth is without both. [221]
Karma that is improperly performed, corrupted by afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) and secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>),
deprived of training (<s>śikṣā</s>), marks [of a renunciant], and so on—some wise ones declare [this]. [222]

children.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau caturthasyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ //
children.translated_text: [In the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s> commentary, the third quarter of the fourth chapter.]
Fourth quarter of the fourth chapter.
From where does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [begin]? From the point where, with irreversible mind,
he girds the armor of enlightenment (<s>bodhi</s>), having undertaken the welfare of the world. [223]
When he performs the characteristic karma, being free from the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>),
of great family, with complete faculties, delighting in gathering his own assembly. [224]
A man, remembering past lives, eloquent, endowed with wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), and action—
then he becomes manifest among gods and humans. [225]
For he, through three incalculable (<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>) [aeons], accumulates the ocean of qualities of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>,
and its basis, the [physical] body, through a hundred <s>kalpas</s>. [226]
Endowed with the thirty-two marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), resplendent with eighty minor signs (<s>vyañjana</s>)—

children.text: dviṣatāmapi yaṃ dṛṣṭvā manaḥ sadyaḥ prasīdati // [227] //
children.translated_text: upon seeing whom, even enemies' minds are immediately gladdened. [227]
The wind at the end of an age [destroys] <s>Meru</s>, fire [destroys] the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>,
the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>) shatters the thunderbolt—yet that mind remains unchanged. [228]
[The first mind] obtained in the desire realm is born in the sixth [heaven], threefold: compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), and succession;

children.text: buddhotpāde naraḥ strī vā tadādyaṃ cittamaśnute // [229] //
children.translated_text: when a <s>Buddha</s> appears, a man or woman attains that first mind (<s>citta</s>). [229]
Giving everything to all at all times for one who speaks—that is the perfection of generosity (<s>dāna</s>);
not abandoning self-control (<s>dama</s>) even at the point of death—that is declared the excellence of moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>). [230]
[Excellence] of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) is through the praise of <s>Tiṣya</s>; of wisdom (<s>dhī</s>) is beyond the diamond-like (<s>vajropama</s>) [concentration];
but the perfection of all is accomplished at the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>). [231]
The three bases of meritorious activity (<s>puṇyakriyāvastu</s>), etc., are the teachings of the means for attaining that;
likewise the four foundations (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) and the teaching of the seven true <s>Dharma</s>s. [232]
Seven yogas, three aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), three trainings (<s>śikṣā</s>), etc., are taught;
likewise, four perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>) are also spoken of in the <s>Vinaya</s>. [233]
The thirty-seven aids to enlightenment (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>) are declared in full by the Self-Born One (<s>Svayambhū</s>);
the causes of all enlightenments are threefold, by mild, etc. [234]
Therefore, there is no other path to enlightenment than the three baskets (<s>piṭakatraya</s>)—<s>sūtra</s>, etc.;
hence, whoever would speak otherwise here, he would be one who speaks against the [true] path. [235]
This is considered the three incalculable [periods] of great <s>kalpas</s>;
the place called 'incalculable' (<s>asaṃkhya</s>) is situated above the lower number. [236]
The appearance of a <s>Jina</s> (Victor) occurs in times of decline, as long as the lifespan is a hundred [years];
of <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s in both [decline and increase]; of <s>Cakravartin</s>s in times of increase. [237]
That [<s>Cakravartin</s>] does not arise below [a lifespan of] eighty thousand [years]; their arising is accepted [only then];
their wheels are of gold, silver, and copper, due to the power of merit (<s>puṇya</s>). [238]
Even when the means of accomplishment are equal, the difference is due to differences in faculties (<s>akṣa</s>), etc.;
like the difference in fruit of giving between a mother seeking worldly existence and one seeking liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). [239]
Due to the excess of cultivation of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), and likewise of one's own awareness and others' awareness,
of the teacher (<s>guru</s>)—likewise that distinction is established. [240]
The greatness of the Teacher (<s>Śāstṛ</s>) is threefold, born from cause (<s>hetu</s>), reality (<s>tattva</s>), and fruit (<s>phala</s>);
even when liberation (<s>vimukti</s>) is equal, [it is distinguished] by the attainment of enlightenment (<s>bodhi</s>) by the three [types]. [241]
In the presence of a <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>'s body is projected;
each mark (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of the <s>Muni</s> is produced from a hundred merits. [242]
Just as the action paths (<s>karmapatha</s>), so the triad of merit (<s>puṇya</s>), etc., is held;
for generosity (<s>dāna</s>) is given by one with regard to one's own benefit, others' benefit, etc. [243]
The karma of body, etc., is the reality thereof; the non-manifest (<s>avijñapti</s>) is again in some cases;
it is declared primarily by the <s>Muni</s> as having great enjoyment (<s>mahābhoga</s>) as its fruit. [244]
Some give gifts for accomplishing their own, others', or both parties' purposes;
others for the continuation of good conduct, not for both parties' purposes. [245]
The excellence of its fruit is remembered due to the distinction of the giver (<s>dātṛ</s>), the gift (<s>vastu</s>), etc.;
the giver, endowed with qualities like faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), gives with proper respect, etc. [246]
Therefore, one obtains fruit endowed with qualities such as reverence;
the gift, complete with color and other qualities, gives fruit such as beauty (<s>saurūpya</s>). [247]
The field (<s>kṣetra</s>) is distinguished by qualities called merit (<s>guṇa</s>), suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), and beneficence (<s>upakāra</s>);
from the mildness of intention (<s>āśaya</s>), etc., [come] mildness, etc., of the karma. [248]
Even to one who gives <s>Dharma</s>, to a child, to a father, to a mother, or to one who is ill—
immeasurable (<s>ameya</s>) is [the merit of giving] to a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and also of giving for another's existence. [249]
That gift of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and also the eighth of another's—
the wise ones have declared that the best is that which is [given] from an <s>Arhat</s> to an <s>Arhat</s>. [250]
Having deliberated, that which is initiated and strengthened through accumulation and so forth,
and is free from counteracting [factors] — that <s>karma</s> is considered 'accumulated' (<s>upacita</s>). [251]
Mental factors [arising] from one's own renunciation and virtuous qualities, in worship of <s>caityas</s> and so forth,
produce fruit even without a recipient, like abiding in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). [252]
The gift of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharma-dāna</s>) by nature has speech as its object, concerning reality, names, and so forth;
because of its indeterminate nature, names and the like are not like the gift of food. [253]
<s>Śīla</s> (moral discipline) is wholesome form (<s>rūpa</s>), explained according to its divisions;
but in the treatise, because of its predominance, it is declared as [leading] to heavenly rebirth. [254]
That which is not corrupted by faults such as immorality, unwholesome roots, and the like,
and which is a factor for the pacification of its opposites — that is called 'pure' (<s>śuddha</s>) here. [255]
The merit that is concentrated here is <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation), because of the cultivation of mind;
primarily for liberation — thus it was declared by the All-Seeing One (<s>Sarvadarśin</s>). [256]
Merit partaking of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and likewise conducive to penetration (<s>nirvedha</s>),
in this teaching, in brief, wholesome roots (<s>śubha-mūla</s>) are declared to be threefold. [257]
Writing, sealing, and calculation are characterized as bodily and vocal <s>karma</s>;
but enumeration should be known as having the nature of mental <s>karma</s>. [258]
Thus ends the fourth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the commentary <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā-vṛtti</s>.
Chapter Five, First Section
The world is inclined toward wrong action and partakes of suffering because of which —
those <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) that bind to existence, such as <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and so forth, I shall now explain. [259]
By specific names arising from activities born of their own powers,
they are referred to by general designations such as <s>anuśaya</s> (latent tendencies) and so forth. [260]
<s>Rāga</s> (attachment), <s>pratigha</s> (aversion), <s>saṃmoha</s> (delusion), <s>māna</s> (pride), <s>kāṅkṣā</s> (doubt), and <s>kudṛṣṭi</s> (wrong views) —
these six are declared as <s>anuśayas</s> (latent tendencies), which obstruct the door to the good. [261]
Through the division of <s>rāga</s>, they are considered seven; through the division of <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (views), they are known as ten;
further, they should be known as ninety-eight through divisions of realm (<s>dhātu</s>), aspect (<s>ākāra</s>), and so forth. [262]
<s>Rāga</s> is divided into two: <s>kāma-rāga</s> (desire-attachment) and that called <s>bhava-rāga</s> (existence-attachment),
mainly due to the distinction of being externally directed or internally dwelling, and so forth. [263]
<s>Satkāya-dṛṣṭi</s> (view of the perishable collection), <s>antagrāha-dṛṣṭi</s> (extreme views), and <s>mithyā-darśana</s> (false view),
<s>dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa</s> (adherence to views) and <s>śīlavrata-parāmarśa</s> (adherence to rules and rituals) — these are the five <s>dṛṣṭis</s> (views). [264]
Here ten are to be abandoned by the insight into suffering (<s>duḥkha-darśana</s>); seven by the insight into the cause (<s>hetu-darśana</s>);
seven are to be abandoned by the insight into cessation (<s>nirodha-darśana</s>); eight by the insight into the path (<s>mārga-darśana</s>). [265]
Because of dependence on what is abandoned by insight (<s>darśana-heya</s>), and because of grasping the aspect of existence,
<s>rāga</s> and the other four should be known as abandoned by both paths. [266]
Views and doubt, arising under the power of conceptualization, are abandoned by insight (<s>darśana</s>);
likewise in the form realm (<s>rūpa-dhātu</s>) and formless realm (<s>ārūpya-dhātu</s>), except for the <s>pratigha</s> (aversion) latent tendency. [267]

children.text: bhavāgre kṣāntiheyā ye dṛggheyā eva te matāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those that are to be abandoned by patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) in the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) are considered as insight-abandonable (<s>darśana-heya</s>);
but those destroyed by knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) in that [realm] are destroyed through practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) alone. [268]

children.text: ahaṃ mameti yā dṛṣṭirasau satkāyadṛk smṛtā /
children.translated_text: The view that [grasps] 'I' and 'mine' is known as <s>satkāya-dṛṣṭi</s> (view of the perishable collection);
the two that grasp its annihilation and permanence are considered <s>antagrāha-dṛṣṭi</s> (extreme views). [269]
That which denies effect and cause is called <s>mithyā-dṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view);
<s>dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa</s> (adherence to views) should be known as grasping inferior things as supreme. [270]
[Grasping] a non-cause [as cause] and a non-path [as path] — that indeed is called <s>śīlavrata-parāmarśa</s> (adherence to rules and rituals);
because of taking a false path through delusion about suffering, it is to be removed by that insight. [271]
The elimination of <s>satkāya-dṛṣṭi</s> is through seeing <s>dharmas</s> alone, and therefore
it occurs at the comprehension of suffering (<s>duḥkhābhisamaya</s>), and thus it is insight-abandonable (<s>darśana-heya</s>). [272]
Two [inversions] arise from <s>dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa</s>, one from <s>satkāya-dṛṣṭi</s>,
and another half from <s>antagrāha-dṛṣṭi</s> — thus are the <s>viparyāsas</s> (inversions) conceived. [273]
From reversed activity of determination and superimposition,
the statement of <s>viparyāsa</s> (inversion) applies only to these, through view, mind, and perception. [274]
There are seven types of <s>māna</s> (pride); from [dividing] three, nine types of pride arise in three ways,
in three ways through self-elevation and so forth — asserting one's own superiority and denying [others']. [275]
Entanglement beginning with envy and so forth, <s>kaukṛtya</s> (remorse), unwholesome types,
and the desire for non-existence of the noble — these arise from the absence of [right] cause. [276]
The establishment of the universal [latent tendencies] is from [the truth of] suffering and [the truth of] origination,
since all those types that are insight-abandonable are established on these two bases. [277]
Doubt, the five views, and ignorance — those [are either] mixed or isolated;
seven are universal (<s>sarvatraga</s>), and from suffering and origination come four [more]. [278]

children.text: dravyato daśa caikaśca nāmnā sapta tu te matāḥ /
children.translated_text: In substance, they are eleven; by name, they are considered seven;
<s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>pratigha</s> (aversion), and <s>māna</s> (pride) operate with discrimination. [279]
Because of operating in another mode, the universal ones pervade all [aspects] at once;
because of depending on [other] realms, the previously stated ones alone are universal. [280]
Nine belong to the upper realms, among those the first [set], except for the two views;
their co-arising <s>dharmas</s>, excluding <s>prāpti</s> (acquisition), are also universal. [281]
Through doubt and wrong view, mixed ignorance, and isolated [ignorance],
these six are to be abandoned by insight into cessation and the path — [abandoned by] the pure vision. [282]
<s>Nirvāṇa</s> is [attained] from one's own level; the path is ninefold in its stages;
the objects of that insight are distinct from each other, being causes and having the nature of causes. [283]
Not <s>rāga</s>, because it lacks causal power [there]; not <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), because there is no offense [there];
not <s>māna</s> (pride), because of extreme tranquility; not the other views, because of their nature. [284]
A universal <s>anuśaya</s> (latent tendency) lies latent in the entirety [of dharmas] within its own realm,
[affecting] its own ground through its own object; but a non-universal one [affects only] its own group. [285]
Because of non-acceptance and being opposed, it does not take the higher levels or the path as its object;
but with regard to its own associated [dharma], not inferior, through association. [286]
By the analogies of the nurse, garment, and stain, and the sequence of sky-dwellers and water-dwellers,
because these lie latent, therefore they are called <s>anuśayas</s> (latent tendencies). [287]
With aspects such as desired and so forth that are distinct, even in atoms and moments,
because they lie latent, therefore they are considered <s>anuśayas</s>. [288]

children.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau pañcamasyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section of the fifth chapter in the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>, in the commentary <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā-vṛtti</s>.
Chapter Five, Second Section
The first two views in the desire realm (<s>kāma-dhātu</s>) are considered covered-indeterminate (<s>nivṛta-avyākṛta</s>);
but in the two [higher] realms, all defilements (<s>mala</s>) are covered-indeterminate. [289]
The rest in the desire realm are unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>), because of <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), and <s>tamas</s> (darkness);
there are indeed three unwholesome roots (<s>akuśala-mūla</s>), through the application of five reasons. [290]
Even for the two [types of] indeterminate, there are three roots, being similar to those;

children.text: avidyā dhīśca tṛṣṇā ca na kāṅkṣāmānadṛṣṭayaḥ // [291] //
children.translated_text: [they are] <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), intelligence (<s>dhī</s>), and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) — not doubt, pride, or views. [291]
Because of instability, upward activity, and non-pervasiveness, respectively,
[those are excluded;] from not fully understanding the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>, [one posits] a non-cause, like one who meditates on rice. [292]
The best among speakers taught four types of question-answers (<s>praśna-vyākaraṇa</s>),
for the purpose of training disciples in debate, and the fourfold [set of] positions. [293]
[They are:] categorical (<s>ekāṃśa</s>), analytical (<s>vibhajya</s>), counter-questioning (<s>paripṛcchā</s>), and that which is to be set aside (<s>sthāpanīya</s>);
like [questions about] death, birth, superiority, the soul, substance, and otherness. [294]
One [position] is designated as advocate of [real] existence (<s>sthāna-vāditva</s>), another is called conceptualization (<s>parikalpa</s>),
another is called [direct] realization (<s>pratipada</s>), and another is designated as advocate of knowledge (<s>jñāna-vāditva</s>). [295]
One who is functioning with active <s>māna</s> (pride), <s>pratigha</s> (aversion), and <s>rāga</s> (attachment),
wherever they have arisen and are not abandoned, is bound (<s>saṃyukta</s>) to that object. [296]
By these mental ones that have not yet arisen, and by all others belonging to one's own time-period,
and likewise by the rest that have not arisen anywhere — the continuum of aggregates (<s>skandha-santati</s>) is bound. [297]
Only two [types] are actually established here; the third is [established] metaphorically,
because of [arguments] from existent and non-existent causes, and because of acceptance by neutral [parties]. [298]
'Everything exists,' 'partially exists,' 'nothing exists,' and another [says]
'the indeterminate exists' — thus four proponents are recognized. [299]

children.text: ebhyo yaḥ prathamo vādī bhajate sādhutāmalau /
children.translated_text: Among these, the first proponent attains correctness without fault;
but the others are mere reasoners, excluded from valid reasoning and scripture. [300]
Because he affirms the three times and the threefold constancy through function,
therefore the first among the four is called <s>Sarvāstivāda</s>. [301]
Two are called <s>bhāvānyathika</s> (change-of-nature), another is <s>avasthānyathika</s> (change-of-state),
and yet another is <s>anyathānyathika</s> (change-of-change) — the third is the reasoner. [302]
He desires to establish the times through function (<s>kāritra</s>);
that [time] in which [a dharma] performs its function is the present; when done, it is past; when not yet done, it is future. [303]
That whose mark is perceived by the intellect is the knowable (<s>saṃjñeya</s>), which is fourfold:
through ultimate [reality] (<s>paramārtha</s>), through convention (<s>saṃvṛtti</s>), through both, and through mutual dependence. [304]
The past exists as unarisen, according to the <s>Buddha</s>'s word, like the present;
and because it is an object of cognitions, its existence is like that of the present. [305]
Cognition does not take a non-existent as its object, [as established] from scripture and reasoning;
in the case of mutual dependence, there is negation of connection, as with a horse's horn. [306]
When a thing such as form has ceased, cognition arises even then;
that [cognition] has a non-existent aspect of knowledge, like the Teacher's knowledge of another's mind. [307]
Because of the occurrence of joy, fear, agitation, memory, and the arising of [their] factors,
through the manifestation of the power of that which has parts — like a lamp, pot, and form. [308]
Because of the goodness of the desire to produce, like the fivefold transformation of existence,
since the subsidiary function of an existent is seen, like a transformation and an attainable action. [309]
A second birth of an already-born entity is not possible;
primary existence [would require] qualities that are absent; secondary existence cannot be found. [310]
birth is accepted as primary for that which bears [its own] characteristic mark, like a child and so forth. [311]
When there is similarity, the usage [of the term] occurs due to that, like calling [something] 'sweet';
The sky would be in bloom with sky-flowers, and the frog would have matted locks,
if the own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of entities were to arise having previously not existed. [312]
<s>Dharmas</s> devoid of the power of stability, with arising accompanied by destruction —

children.text: vada somya kathaṃ yāti pratītyā vastu vastutām // [313] //
children.translated_text: tell me, dear one, how does a thing attain thingness through dependent [arising]? [313]
In the world, mutual assistance is seen only among existents;
likewise obstruction — not between horse's horns and snakes, and such [non-existent things]. [314]
That which arises dependently does not exist by its own nature;
[but] what does not exist by own-nature — if it does not exist, then it is otherwise [than alleged]. [315]
Causes produce merely a [new] condition of an entity that exists,
like the kingship of a prince [is produced] by ministers who possess a self. [316]
When there is an assemblage of <s>dharmas</s>, capability arises,
just as for atoms that are accumulated, in the perception of a self. [317]
[If you say] past <s>karma</s> is non-existent, and the non-existent produces a future result that is [also] non-existent,
then clearly a barren woman's son would be born from the child of an intermediate being. [318]
Because of the absence of a valid characteristic for a name, and because of the establishment of the mark of substantial reality (<s>dravya-satya</s>),
the future and past do not have merely conventional reality (<s>prajñapti-satya</s>). [319]

children.text: ko vighnaḥ aṅgavaikalyam na tatsarvāstitā sadā /
children.translated_text: What is the obstruction? [It is] deficiency of factors — that [universal existence] is not always [applicable];

children.text: tatkathaṃ śrūyatāṃ sadbhyaḥ durbodhā khalu dharmatā // [320] //
children.translated_text: how then? Listen, O noble ones — the nature of <s>dharmas</s> is indeed difficult to comprehend. [320]
From the conjunction with the present time, through the coming together of the factors of the assemblage,
the projection of a result by one that has obtained power is called function (<s>kāritra</s>). [321]
Present-ness is not [a dharma's] form, nor is past-ness or future-ness;
therefore, it is not through traversal of time-periods that form's nature is considered to change. [322]
A certain state arises for an existing entity;

children.text: tathā śaktistathā velā tathā sattā tathā kriyā // [323] //
children.translated_text: likewise power, likewise occasion, likewise existence, likewise activity. [323]
The world is pervaded by conceptualizations that delight the minds of fools;
but that conceptualization which grasps the mind of the wise — that is rare. [324]
Bound by the other universals, when what is to be abandoned by the insight into suffering is destroyed,
even when the earlier type is destroyed, [one is still bound] by the remaining ones that depend on it. [325]
Sixteen should be known, each having the nature of three existences;

children.text: dharmāḥ pañcadhā nirmalāścaiva vijñānāni tathaiva ca // [326] //
children.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s> [are classified] in five ways, as well as the pure ones, and likewise the consciousnesses (<s>vijñāna</s>). [326]
One should examine them in [terms of] elements (<s>dhātu</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), truths (<s>satya</s>), and [their] modes,
as prompted by the collection of <s>dharmas</s>, consciousness, knowledge, and latent tendencies. [327]
Those to be abandoned by insight into suffering and its cause, belonging to the desire realm, [and those] destroyed by meditation —
attaining a single form through their own triad, dispassionate, having mind as their domain. [328]
But those born of form among the pure ones, [along with] one's own and the lower three, [combined with] one upper —
those belonging to the formless realm, the triad belonging to the three realms — these are the objects of the pure. [329]
All should be known as belonging to their own and higher [levels]; those with equal liberation are destroyed by insight;
the afflictions belonging to the three existences, the last triad — these are the objects of the pure. [330]
That belonging to the desire realm has five objects; that belonging to the form realm has eight objects;
that belonging to the formless realm has ten [objects], and the pure also has ten. [331]
The desire-realm [defilements] regarding <s>dharma</s> and meaning in the upper [realm], in consciousness — three belong to their own level;
those belonging to the form realm, to be abandoned by meditation, being universal, lie latent. [332]

children.text: catvāraḥ parivṛtte sve rūpāptāḥ khalvapi trayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Four [lie latent] in their own transformed [state]; three indeed belong to the form realm;
those belonging to the formless realm, together with the universals, are destroyed by meditation. [333]
Likewise also in the second, and in the fifth also similarly;
those with defiled objects lie latent in their own [realm] and also in the third. [334]
But in the transformed [state], those belonging to the desire realm, depending on conditioned objects —
the rest should be explained as before; in the fourth also, as in the third. [335]
But in the transformed [state], four belonging to the desire realm; elsewhere, as before.

children.text: rūpāpte prathame 'dhastāt trayaḥ sve khalvapi trayaḥ // [336] //
children.translated_text: For one obtained in the form realm, in the first [truth], three from below, and indeed three in one's own [realm]. [336]
In the case of conversion, three from below and four from one's own realm. [337]
Those of the formless realm, together with the universal ones, [are] to be abandoned by the path of <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation),
And the four groups obtained from the formless realm lie latent.
Likewise in the second [truth] and in the fifth [faculty] too. [338]
Those having impure objects in one's own [realm] lie latent in the third also,
But in the case of conversion, those obtained in the form realm that have conditioned objects [lie latent]. [339]
The rest should be known as before; in the fourth also, as in the third.
In the case of conversion, as in the third; one should understand [this] regarding the first formless [realm]. [340]
In one's own [realm] three, those obtained from the desire realm, and three groups of three obtained from the form realm,
In the case of conversion, as for those obtained in the form realm; likewise in the second and fifth. [341]
In the third also, in one's own [realm], those having impure objects,
In the case of conversion, those obtained from one's own realm that have conditioned objects. [342]
The rest should be stated as in the first; in the fourth also, as in the third.
But in the case of conversion, as in the first; the wise one should indicate [this] regarding consciousness. [343]
The group to be abandoned by the path of <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation), together with the universal ones,
Lies latent—obtained from two realms, excluding the formless—in the eye faculty (<s>cakṣurindriya</s>). [344]
The groups obtained from the desire and form realms, in the domain of the eye faculty,
Those to be abandoned by seeing suffering and [its] cause, and by practice—three groups of three. [345]
Those of the formless realm, to be abandoned by <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation), and the universal ones, lie latent,
But in the case of conversion, four, excluding the seeing of cessation. [346]

children.text: duḥkhendriye tu kāmāptaḥ svaireva saha sarvagaiḥ /
children.translated_text: But regarding the faculty of suffering (<s>duḥkhendriya</s>), [the group] obtained from the desire realm, together with its own universal ones,
The groups lie latent in the consciousness that has that [faculty] as its domain. [347]
Three obtained from the desire realm, [three from] the form [realm], those to be abandoned by universal practice,
But in the case of conversion, four obtained from the desire realm lie latent. [348]
Three from the form realm, the last [realm], those universal ones to be abandoned by <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation),
All four lie latent in the case of double conversion. [349]
In the faculty of pleasure (<s>sukhendriya</s>), in the mind having that as its object, and in [the consciousness] that has that as its domain,
Those obtained from the desire realm and so forth, as appropriate, and the universal ones lie latent. [350]
But all those comprised in the three realms, in the mental faculty (<s>manasindriya</s>),
In the consciousness that has that as its object, with all conditioned phenomena as their domain. [351]
Only those having conditioned objects lie latent in the case of conversion,
There is no difference here in the case of double conversion. [352]
From the mind to be abandoned by seeing suffering and so forth, the minds of a being in the desire realm,

children.text: bhavatyanantaraṃ ṣaḍ vā tasyodardhvaṃ pañca pañca vā // [353] //
children.translated_text: Become immediately six, or above that, five or five. [353]
But for one born in the form realm, one should specify the minds,

children.text: ekaṃ vā pañca vā ṣaḍ vā sapta vā yadi vā daśa // [354] //
children.translated_text: As one, or five, or six, or seven, or ten. [354]
