For one born in the formless realm, one should note these minds,
Five only of one's own realm; at the time of death, ten from elsewhere. [355]
A mind is considered to be 'with latent defilement' (<s>sānuśaya</s>) due to association and due to the nature of being a latent defilement.
Or twofold—defiled and undefiled—it is designated as one only. [356]
From delusion (<s>moha</s>) arises the view of the real self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), from that arises the extreme view (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>),
From that, doubt (<s>kāṅkṣā</s>) and wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>); from that view comes clinging to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>). [357]
Attachment (<s>rāga</s>) arises regarding one's own view, pride (<s>māna</s>) also, and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) extends to other [views].
This sequence of these [defilements] should be known thus, due to the predominance of their arising. [358]
But due to association with good and bad friends, their activity is considered to be unrestricted.
A <s>kleśa</s> (defilement) arises with three complete causes. [359]

children.text: abhidharmadīpe vibhāṣāprabhāyāṃ vṛttau pañcamasyādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the second section of the fifth chapter in the <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s> commentary on the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>.
Third section of the fifth chapter.

children.text: vyavidyāḥ sakalāḥ kleśāḥ kāme kāmāsravo mataḥ /
children.translated_text: All defilements that are non-ignorance in the desire realm are considered the outflow of desire (<s>kāmāsrava</s>),
And excluding torpor (<s>styāna</s>) and restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), those above [the desire realm] are the outflow of existence (<s>bhavāsrava</s>), due to their uniformity. [360]
But ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), being the root, is the outflow of ignorance, pervading all realms,
Likewise the floods (<s>ogha</s>) and yokes (<s>yoga</s>), excluding views; their separate treatment is due to their force. [361]

children.text: sāvidyā dve upādāne yathākto(ktau) dve tu dṛṅmaye /
children.translated_text: Two clinging factors (<s>upādāna</s>) include ignorance as stated, and two consist of views,
Although four, one is the last one, due to reliance on wrong path and so forth. [362]
The remaining ones belong to all three realms; in the last, due to the activity regarding selfhood,
They are shown again in five ways by terms such as fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) and so forth. [363]
In this [system] there are nine fetters, as well as envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) and miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>).
Due to the commonality of substance and intolerance, views constitute two [kinds of] fetters. [364]
The remaining [five] latent defilements (<s>anuśaya</s>), again fivefold in each of the five,
Are declared as the lower fetters (<s>avarabhāgīya</s>) and the upper fetters (<s>ūrdhvabhāgīya</s>). [365]

children.text: ādyantye dve dṛśau kāṃkṣā(kāṅkṣā)kāmacchando dvireva yaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the first [set], the last two views, doubt (<s>kāṅkṣā</s>), and desire for sensual pleasure (<s>kāmacchanda</s>) which is twofold,
By two [fetters] one does not transcend the desire realm; by three there is return. [366]
Due to the statement of the function of two and one to be abandoned by seeing, and due to grasping the chief among those to be abandoned by seeing,
Even though all are to be abandoned by seeing, these three are specified. [367]
Due to being the cause of all misfortune, due to being opposed to the path,
And due to being devoid of true reasoning, there is the teaching of three fetters (<s>trisaṃyojana</s>). [368]
Two attachments born of the form and formless realms, and three arising from pride (<s>māna</s>), delusion (<s>moha</s>), and restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>),
Due to being latent in three feelings, and due to firmness, there are three bonds (<s>bandhana</s>). [369]
Due to binding in two ways, four knots (<s>grantha</s>) are declared,
Namely covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and the two [kinds of] clinging (<s>parāmarśa</s>). [370]
The secondary defilements (<s>upakleśa</s>) should be known as anger and so forth, as stated,
Or all defiled mental factors designated as belonging to the aggregate of formations (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>). [371]
Others, being the impurities of the root defilements, are designated as six secondary defilements (<s>upakleśa</s>),
Namely deceit (<s>śāṭhya</s>), enmity (<s>upanāha</s>), spite (<s>pradāśa</s>), guile (<s>māyā</s>), intoxication (<s>mada</s>), and cruelty (<s>viheṭhanā</s>). [372]

Concealment (<s>mrakṣa</s>), envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>), torpor (<s>styāna</s>), drowsiness (<s>middha</s>), restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>),
Miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>), and regret (<s>kaukṛtya</s>)—these are the ten wrappings (<s>paryavasthāna</s>). [373]
Shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), and so forth are outflows of those [root defilements],
Concealment (<s>mrakṣa</s>), lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>), torpor (<s>styāna</s>), drowsiness (<s>middha</s>), and so forth arise from delusion (<s>moha</s>). [374]
Regret (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) arises from doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>); anger (<s>krodha</s>) and so forth arise from aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>),
Heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>), rigidity (<s>stambha</s>), lassitude, guile (<s>māyā</s>), deceit (<s>śāṭhya</s>), and yawning (<s>vijṛmbhikā</s>). [375]
Bodily heaviness (<s>kāyadauṣṭhulya</s>) and so forth should be known as arising from mixed [causes].
Spite (<s>pradāśa</s>) is an outflow of clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>); deceit (<s>śaṭhatā</s>) is [an outflow] of views. [376]
The association of attachment (<s>rāga</s>) is with mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>) and with bodily pleasure (<s>sukha</s>),
And the [association] of aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) is declared to be with mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) and with bodily pain (<s>duḥkha</s>). [377]
Delusion (<s>moha</s>) [is associated] with all [feelings]; the false view with two mental [feelings],
And doubt (<s>kāṅkṣā</s>) with mental displeasure; the remaining ones with mental pleasure. [378]
But with equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) [all are associated]—this is the rule for those obtained in the desire realm.
But for those born in other realms, [they are associated] with their own [feelings] at each level. [379]
Envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) [is associated] with mental displeasure, likewise regret (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) and anger (<s>krodha</s>),
As well as spite (<s>pradāśa</s>), enmity (<s>upanāha</s>), and cruelty (<s>vihiṃsā</s>). [380]
Miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>) [is associated] with mental displeasure; some [say] with mental pleasure,

children.text: dvābhyāṃ māyā tathā śāṭhyaṃ mrakṣo middhaṃ tathaiva ca // [381] //
children.translated_text: Guile (<s>māyā</s>), deceit (<s>śāṭhya</s>), concealment (<s>mrakṣa</s>), and drowsiness (<s>middha</s>) with both [feelings]. [381]
But intoxication (<s>mada</s>) is associated with mental pleasure and bodily pleasure,
Shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>), torpor (<s>styāna</s>), and restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>) with all five [feelings]. [382]
Shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>), torpor (<s>styāna</s>), drowsiness (<s>middha</s>), and likewise restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>). [383]
..........[This is the third section of the fifth chapter in the <s>Vibhāṣāprabhā</s> commentary on the <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s>.
] ..........[The fifth chapter is concluded.]
